_meta.what_this_is: A set of color patches, each an [R, G, B] byte triple, used to compare two ways of collapsing a color to a single brightness: the naive unweighted average (R+G+B)/3 and the perceptual Rec. 709 luma 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B. The three primaries (red, green, blue) are the crux: the average gives all three the identical value 85, while luma spreads them across their true perceived range. A short colored image strip is included to show grayscale conversion.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The colors are hand-authored so the collapse (all primaries to 85 under the average) and the perceptual ordering (green > red > blue under luma) are exact and checkable; every brightness is computed in luma.py from the Rec. 709 weights, nothing is precomputed.
_meta.format: patches: [{name, rgb}]; image: a list of [R,G,B] pixels for the grayscale demo.
